identity.title: Nephrotoxin and contrast exposure history (NSAID, ACEi/ARB, diuretic, aminoglycoside, vancomycin, PPI, iodinated contrast; timing)

technique.how: Reconcile all drugs against the chart and pharmacy record, including over-the-counter NSAIDs and herbal products: NSAIDs, ACEi/ARB, diuretics, aminoglycosides, vancomycin (with piperacillin-tazobactam), PPIs, and any iodinated contrast. For each, record start date, dose change and timing relative to the creatinine rise.
technique.prerequisites: Access to medication administration and imaging records; collateral history for patients who cannot report OTC use.

interpretation.positive_finding: A nephrotoxin started or dosed within days of the creatinine rise, or contrast within 48-72 h, makes drug-induced AKI (hemodynamic, ATN or AIN) a leading candidate and identifies an immediately reversible factor.
interpretation.negative_finding: No exposure lowers the likelihood of drug-related AKI and contrast nephropathy, redirecting attention to hypovolemia, sepsis, obstruction and intrinsic renal disease.
interpretation.pitfalls: Patients under-report OTC NSAIDs; PPI-associated AIN can begin weeks to months after the start; contrast-associated AKI is often confounded by the illness that prompted imaging, so timing alone does not prove causation.
interpretation.changes_what: A positive exposure history should lead to stopping or dose-adjusting the agent, avoiding further nephrotoxins and monitoring creatinine; still assess obstruction and volume status.

sources.citation: Khwaja A. KDIGO clinical practice guidelines for acute kidney injury. Nephron Clin Pract. 2012;120(4):c179-c184 (summary of the KDIGO 2012 AKI guideline).

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not attribute AKI solely to a drug or contrast when there is oliguria, sepsis, hypotension or possible obstruction; these still need evaluation.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: AKI with hyperkalemia, acidosis, fluid overload or uremic symptoms needs urgent nephrology review regardless of the exposure history.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: History accuracy depends on medication reconciliation quality; structured pharmacy review captures more exposures than patient recall.

extraction_notes: No diagnostic-accuracy study reports sensitivity/specificity/LR of a nephrotoxin or contrast exposure history for AKI etiology; the exposures are causal risk factors, so the record is not_quantified and cites the KDIGO 2012 AKI guideline (Khwaja summary, PMID 22890468; PubMed lists year 2015 for the record, print citation is 2012). The Kidney Int Suppl DOI 10.1038/kisup.2012.1 resolved via Crossref to a 'Notice' front-matter item, not the guideline, so it was not cited. Search budget spent on the seeded anchor; no additional PubMed searches were run for this id.
